messages.subject: Issue with write.im3d
parts:
Hello all,

i've been having some issues with the write.im3d function. I have read neurons into R and transformed them to various brain registrations. I'm now looking to convert these to .nrrd files, but have been getting an unexpected error which I haven't been able to solve: 

neuron <- neuprint_read_neurons(5813046951, heal = TRUE, heal.threshold = 1e9, connectors=FALSE)
neuron.JRC2018U <- xform_brain(neuron*8/1000, reference=JRC2018U, sample="JRCFIB2018F")
im <- as.im3d(xyzmatrix(neuron.JRC2018U), JRC2018U)
write.im3d(im, "5813011145.nrrd")

with this code, I get the error message:
Error in writeBin(as.vector(x, mode = dmode), fc, size = dtypesize, endian = endian) : 
  only 2^31-1 bytes can be written in a single writeBin() call

This error occurs while testing a number of other neurons. I've also tried using write.nrrd but I still get the error.

Does anyone have any ideas on what might be causing the error and how to work around it? Would be very grateful for the help.

Thanks,
Rory

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Issue with write.im3d
parts:
Dear Rory,

That means that your image dimensions are too large for the current code:

2^31
[1] 2147483648

i.e. ~2GB 

> (2^31)^(1/3)
[1] 1290.159

So the limit is about 1290 x 1290 x 1290 or the same product with a different side ratio. I personally have not had to deal with images of this size in R. My first suggestion is to consider slightly increasing your voxel size. If that's not an option then the code needs to be modified. This is the place:

https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461

I don't have time to do this just now, but if you want to try and have a go by cloning the nat repo, I think something like the below should work (untested). I'd also recommend making a GitHub issue 

https://github.com/natverse/nat/issues

All the best,

Greg.

# add a new function

#' Split slices of an image into chunks based on maximum integer index size
#'
#' @details in R linear indices into arrays can only be 2^31 long (32 bit int).
#'   This means that \code{writeBin} can only write this many pixels in one go.
#'   Therefore to write bigger pixel arrays, you must split the images into chunks
#'   for writing. NB this function currently only works for 3D arrays.
#'
#' @param x An array containing image data
#' @param max_chunk_size (default is max for writeBin)
#'
#' @return a vector of length the number of slices, giving the chunk index (1:nchunks) 
#'   for each slice.
make_image_chunks <- function(x, max_chunk_size=2^31-1) {
  lastdim=length(dim(x))
  # FIXME handle arrays that are not 3D
  stopifnot(lastdim==3)
  nslices=dim(x)[lastdim]
  slice_size=prod(dim(x)[-lastdim])
  if(slice_size>max_chunk_size)
    stop("write.nrrd cannot write data with slices with > 2^31 pixels")
  slices_per_chunk=1 + (max_chunk_size %/% slice_size)
  chunk_size=slices_per_chunk * slice_size
  nchunks=1 + nslices %/% slices_per_chunk
  #
  chunks=rep(seq_len(nchunks), rep(slices_per_chunk, nchunks))[seq_len(nslices)]
  chunks
}

# edit these lines:
# https://github.com/natverse/nat/blob/4d85cc7a2ea66cecd0576c0ff2fe96be722a5341/R/nrrd-io.R#L459-L461

fc=ifelse(enc=="gzip", gzfile, base::file)(file, open=fmode)
if(length(x)>=2^31 && max(chunks <- make_image_chunks(x))>1) {
  # too big, must chunk
  for(i in seq_len(max(chunks))) {
    writeBin(as.vector(x[, , chunks == i], mode = dmode),

fc,
             size = dtypesize,
             endian = endian)
  }

} else {
  # write in one go
  writeBin(as.vector(x, mode=dmode), fc, size=dtypesize, endian=endian)
}
close(fc)

messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] Issue with write.im3d
parts:
Dear Jon,

If you fancy trying your hand at coding, I have posted most of the solution below.

That said, if your goal is to co-display neurons and volume data, there may be better solutions

1. You can use simple neurite tracer to display SWC files in Fiji in slice or 3d view.

2. You can use https://github.com/takashi310/VVD_Viewer (a fork of fluorender) to generate high quality volumetric rendering in conjunction with an SWC

Other options include

* Vaa3D
* Amira (commercial, but we've used this a lot in the past. This package might be helpful https://github.com/jefferis/nat.amira)
* Paraview (if you write your neuron to VTK format with write.neurons(nl, format='vtk')) 

Best,

Greg.
